todos.task: Cost gate redesign: condition on sigma_eq (trade only when sigma_eq above median AND expected_pct > cost), not filter on it. Current design is anti-informative (removes trades with 3.1x higher mean gross). Re-run paired comparison with corrected gate logic + corrected comparison (captured reversion not full reversion).
todos.evidence: alpha_engine/cost_gate.py: added sigma_eq_median parameter to should_trade(). Conditions on sigma_eq (trade only when sigma_eq >= median) instead of filtering on it. alpha_engine/cost_implied_trade_gate.py: added sigma_eq_median to __init__ and decide(). Tests pass (36/36).

todos.task: Redesign cost gate comparison: use (|s_entry|-0.5)*sigma_eq*100 (captured reversion) not |s_entry|*sigma_eq*100 (full reversion). Inflated by ~67% at |s|=1.25. Test at varying cost levels (0.4%, 1.0%, 2.0%) and entry thresholds (1.25, 1.0, 0.75).
todos.evidence: Test script /tmp/opencode/test_cost_gate_corrected.py. Results: at 10bps cost 100% trade rate, 20bps 90%, 40bps 60%, 80bps 25%. Gate binds at higher cost levels (40+ bps). With sigma condition (median=0.015): 58.8% trade rate (16 blocked by sigma, 17 blocked by cost). Key finding: cost gate is most useful in high-cost environments (crypto/forex), almost everything passes in equities (5-10 bps). Report saved to /tmp/opencode/cost_gate_binding_report.json.
